subject.title: Exec allowlist matches never auto-execute on darwin — "allowlist auto-execution is unavailable on darwin; reviewer or explicit approval is required" (2026.6.11)

question: For macOS gateway exec, should matched shell-shaped allowlist commands auto-execute when OpenClaw can safely materialize an enforced plan, or should the current plan-miss prompt be the supported security boundary?
rationale: The issue sits on an exec security boundary: restoring silent execution improves shipped automation behavior, but the wrong repair could execute raw shell text that differs from the allowlist-resolved target.

options.title: Fix enforceable macOS matches
options.body: Repair only the shell shapes that can be safely rendered into an enforced command, add macOS-focused regression coverage, and keep plan-miss prompts for the rest.

options.title: Document prompt-only plan misses
options.body: Keep the current fail-closed approval behavior and update exec approval docs plus the warning to explain command-shape causes such as tilde expansion.

options.title: Allow raw matched shell text
options.body: Permit all matched macOS allowlist commands to run without an enforced plan, accepting a larger shell-resolution security risk.

recommendation.title: Fix enforceable macOS matches
recommendation.body: Repair only the shell shapes that can be safely rendered into an enforced command, add macOS-focused regression coverage, and keep plan-miss prompts for the rest.

likelyOwner.reason: The current gate and recent exec approval boundary work are most directly tied to this history.
